The Treasury Department declines to comment to the FT for its report on the entity list

Tells the FT it does not comment on internal discussions about the entity list; the department says it has "enforced aggressively across the board, including on smuggling advanced chips" and cites six investigations with "criminal charges against 17 defendants"
Implicator: beside its denial of the confrontation, the department "would not immediately comment on the other allegations"

A spokeswoman tells the Times the department does not comment on continuing investigations; it declines to comment to NBC, and the FBI declines to comment to AFP and to Semafor on the president's remark that it is looking into the matter
The FBI declines to comment when the BBC asks, as a Ukrainian outlet relays it; Yahoo Finance also reports an FBI refusal, without saying who asked

Bloomberg, as Quartz relays it: the department "is examining whether entities tied to Alice Huang ... had a hand in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer's products into China"; the U.S. attorney's office in Manhattan leads; the department and that office had no comment. Quartz adds that Jensen Huang "is not a target of U.S. law enforcement probes", and that it "remains uncertain" whether the inquiry connects to any smuggling prosecution and what part Alice Huang or her entities had
Declines to comment to the Times for its profile of Alice Huang

Says customer meetings are "part of a CEO's job" and that customers get "zero information relevant to national security"; a spokesman tells the Times Huang "has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed"; the spokesman declines to comment on whether Huang will appear before the committees

A spokesman tells the Times the company does not share classified information with its customers, and that customers do not ask it to press the government to change its policies on chip sales to China; China has "consistently promoted its own domestic alternatives in China, including Huawei, and strictly limited imports of our data center products". To the FT, for its report of that day, the company "declined to comment on the government memo and the assertions that its chief executive had an intimate relationship with Alice Huang"

At its event in Seoul that day, asked about the investigation and Korea's chip purchases, declines to comment: "Those questions don't seem to be related to today's event" (Asia Economy). A spokesman declines to comment to the Times, which asked on Monday for its report on succession and the board. To the FT it declines to comment on remarks the paper attributes to its general counsel
Declines to comment to the Times for its profile of Alice Huang
Declines to give the Times a statement for its report of a second relationship; declines to comment for another Times article and for an FT report of that day

Has declined to say how Megaspeed's sales were classified after it changed how it reports revenue by country, in the Journal's account; Implicator adds that the filings "do not establish a connection between the reporting change and the block". Declines to comment to the FT, the Journal and Reuters for other reports of that day
A State Department spokesman declines to comment to the Times for its report on his memo
Says he "can't comment on an internal corporate matter that's going on with Nvidia". NBC has him "speaking Sunday"; a republished transcript of the exchange is titled 9 November

Asked again about Huang and how important a thorough investigation is: "I'm not going to comment on an internal corporate matter for them"; asked whether he sees a national security concern: "I'm just not going to comment on it". The republished transcript is titled 10 November and stamped the evening of Nov 9, Eastern time
The State Department declines to comment to the Times for its report that the president was told of the concerns on his trip to China

Denies the Journal's account of Alice Huang: "no such investigations"; its police say the Megaspeed inquiry continues, that they are "unable to comment further at this juncture", and that they "act firmly against companies and individuals who violate our laws". The statement is timed Oct 30, 11:13 PM in Singapore; the ministry's newsroom page dates it Oct 31
Its representative office in Washington tells the Journal it "doesn't comment on specific intelligence or security matters"

At the legislature its interior minister says "The national security authorities are actively investigating, and the Ministry of the Interior is cooperating" (Asia Economy, from a Taiwanese daily). Its premier declines to answer a question about Taiwan's part in the U.S. investigation; he says the government has records of her entries and exits and "would not say how many times she had visited" (Taiwan News)

Its deputy foreign minister says she complied with entry rules and that the government is taking the necessary precautions, in Asia Economy's account of Nov 10; he declines to tell reporters under what status she entered (Taiwan News)

Its China-policy agency, of a U.S. recommendation in 2024 to monitor her visits that the Times reported: "MAC has indeed never received such information"; "We are not sure whether other agencies received it". The cabinet's spokesperson calls the case a cross-border cooperative investigation and declines to give details, citing the confidentiality of ongoing investigations; the immigration agency says it worked with security authorities to monitor her visits (Focus Taiwan)

Asked whether he knew of the concerns when Huang flew with him to China in May: "No, I didn't hear about it then"; pressed on whether he had been briefed a year earlier: "I'd certainly check with the intelligence people. They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn't make much of an impact on me" (the Times). The Journal: he "declined to provide a detailed explanation of when he learned about the federal government's concerns"
With the CIA and the National Security Agency, declines to comment to the Times for its first report
With the CIA, declines to comment to the Times and to the FT for their reports of the memo
A spokeswoman declines to comment to the Times for its report on the secretary of state's memo

Declines to comment to the FT for its report on the entity list.
